source_refs.locator: Results §3.1 and Table 2, community-specific climate impacts and relocation status

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-09-04 reports: Floods, cyclones and erosion damaged homes and land across the seven sites; flooding cut road access in Vunivau, Nacekoro and Dratabu, salt intrusion affected Vunidogoloa, and river erosion limited Matawalu farmland.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-09-04 reports: In March 2024, Matawalu, Nawaqarua and Nacekoro lacked relocation consensus; Vunivau and Nabavatu awaited government support, with procedural delay and tent shelters noted at Nabavatu.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-09-04 reports: Nawaqarua used early-warning alarms and drainage; Nacekoro planted mangroves and vetiver. Walls were sought at Matawalu, Nacekoro and Nawaqarua, but some walls elsewhere blocked drainage or prolonged floods.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Physical PDF pp.9–10, printed pp.6–7, Box 1.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-06 reports: IMF summarizes post-flood household surveys in Votua, Nawaqarua and Etatoko showing mixed relocation views; land ties, livelihoods, limited productive land and amenities, and tenure constrained resettlement; an Etatoko plantation lease was shortened for relocating households.

source_refs.locator: Full text, Results: knowledge of climatic risks and environmental security

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-06 reports: Residents of Vunidogoloa, Cakaudrove Province, recalled coastal and river flooding, erosion, rising tides and waves, salt intrusion and food insecurity; 26 households, about 140 people, relocated roughly 1 km inland in 2014 after seawalls failed.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Full text, Discussion and Results on environmental risks, resources and services

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-06 reports: After moving, residents reported less coastal-flood exposure and better water, sanitation, schools and health access, but new cyclone and heat exposure, incomplete paths and drainage, and reduced fishing access, especially for women and older people.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Full text, Local agency and participation; Discussion of relocation monitoring

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-06 reports: The relocation was community-initiated and led through village governance; later, residents reported no ongoing government or donor monitoring or formal channel for unfinished construction concerns, while the women’s committee continued village development work.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related relocation may interact with tenure, consent and trust to create disputes; Fiji evidence supports a conditional risk mechanism, not climate-caused violence.
alternative_explanations: Housing policy, development-led relocation, service inequality, policing and generational preferences may drive disputes independently of climate.
pathways.uncertainty: Prospective source-stated mechanism with qualitative local examples; no causal estimate or current legal interpretation.
recommendations: Retain only evidence whose documented geography supports the pathway location; otherwise narrow the pathway or keep the evidence standalone.
